Science.title: A cactus that changes gears: How the prickly pear makes the most of desert rain
Science.summary: In the desert, water doesn't arrive steadily. It comes in short pulses: a winter storm, a few rainy days, then months of drought. A desert plant needs two skills to live there. It has to survive the long dry spells, and it has to make full use of the brief windows when water is plentiful. A new study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and the Volcani Institute shows that the prickly pear cactus has an unexpected way of doing both.

Science.title: Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman

Science.title: Which pollen is found in honey? Automated analysis closely matches conventional testing
Science.summary: Pure rapeseed honey—or not quite? Single-flower honeys must contain a certain proportion of pollen from the respective plant. Science.title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs
Science.summary: A quantum device with more qubits is harder to verify. Describing a general quantum state takes an exponential number of parameters, and reconstructing it in full—a procedure known as state tomography—becomes impractical as the system grows. Yet most experiments do not need the full description. They need to know a few things: Is the state close to the target? Are the qubits entangled? And does the system carry the resources needed for quantum computation?

Science.title: Stellar pulses reveal hidden binary in JWST calibration star sample
Science.summary: Stars used to calibrate the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) must have precisely characterized spectra so that their fluxes can be measured accurately. Yet some stars that appear single may in fact harbor unresolved companions that alter their predicted radiation. One such object, HD 158485—an A-type star in the JWST calibration program—has now been shown to be a binary system whose two stars both pulsate.

Science.title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses
Science.summary: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. A new study by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) uncovers the inner workings of the poxvirus core: how its gene-copying machines sit parked in dormant pairs, ready to print viral instructions and release them into the host cell through dedicated export portals embedded in the core shell.
